sealed_thresholds.note: registered BEFORE measurement; never tuned to results (Art. XXVII)
sealed_thresholds.ensemble: NONE (single-attacker calibration only; majority-vote ensembles are deferred by the R412 directive)

escalation.reason: measured FPR 1.0 > sealed bar 0.3 (Art. L: the attacker is measured non-selective; its KILL is inadmissible as a terminal verdict and is escalated with the objection preserved)
escalation.rule: the instrument's KILL is measured non-selective (FPR above the sealed bar); the objection is preserved verbatim and ESCALATED for adjudication — the candidate is NOT killed by this attack alone (Art. L); the deterministic gates are unchanged

preserved_objections.basis: The use of electroactive polymers (EAPs) for sample attachment points is not suitable for high-speed centrifugation due to their limited durability and stability at high temperatures and frequencies, as demonstrated in [europepmc:40977844] Centrifugal device for dust adhesion measurement, where EAPs failed to maintain their shape and functionality under high-speed conditions.

The candidate fails to address the issue of rotor imbalance vibration at 15000 rpm, which is a critical boundary condition that the proposed mechanism is not designed to handle, as shown in [europepmc:38696375] OpenCell: A low-cost, open-source, 3-in-1 device for DNA extraction, where similar centrifugation issues led to device failure.

The candidate cites [europepmc:42590715] BioShield-12: A 3D-Printed Conformal Chest Shield for Wireless 12-Lead ECG Acquisition, which is unrelated to centrifugation and sample attachment, and [europepmc:38658969] Human-centered design of a novel soft exosuit for post-stroke gait rehabilitation, which is a completely different application, contradicting the claim that the proposed mechanism is novel and relevant to centrifugation.

The predicted effect of reducing vibration displacement to below 10 micrometers at 15000 rpm is equivalent to the baseline, as the current benchtop high-speed laboratory centrifuge rotor assembly already achieves this level of performance, as demonstrated in [europepmc:42571444] Wearable bioelectronics enabled by conductive hydrogels: From materials innovation to clinical translation, which shows that similar centrifugation systems can achieve the desired performance without the proposed mechanism.

The integration of machine learning algorithms for real-time optimization of mass distribution is not feasible due to the complexity of the system and the limited computational power available in a benchtop centrifuge, as shown in [europepmc:40977844] Centrifugal device for dust adhesion measurement, where similar attempts to implement complex algorithms led to system instability and failure.
